comment: Snapshot of the advertised broker-front list and the order discovery races it in. Consumed by four suites over two repos — Go (contract/broker_fronts_test.go, against brokerapi's DefaultBrokerURLs, BrokerCandidates, and EndpointUnboundBrokerFront) in this repo, and Kotlin, Swift, and Jest in openrung-mobile-app, which vendors this file and checks the vendored copy against a pinned openrung ref. A front that silently disappears from one client is a front that client cannot fall back to when the others are blocked, so an existing entry may only change together with a bump of 'version' here and in every vendored copy, so the change lands in all four suites at once. Rotating or adding a front is exactly such a change.
phase_note: Discovery races the fronts in two phases. Phase 1 holds every front whose TLS connection authenticates that endpoint. Phase 2 starts only after every phase-1 front has failed, and holds fronts dialed without SNI onto a shared CDN edge whose certificate proves only 'an edge of this provider', never this endpoint — the Ed25519 relay-list signature is what makes them trustworthy, so they are tried last. A front is assigned to a phase by the shape of its hostname, not by matching this deployment's own endpoints, so a fork or a rotated endpoint is classified the same way.

classification.note: Dialed without SNI, but the CloudFront distribution still serves this deployment's own certificate, so the connection authenticates the endpoint.
Matched by hostname shape: the bare Front Door endpoint form.
And the zoned form, where the zone is a letter followed by two digits.
Not a zone shape (two letters), so it is not the shared-edge path.
A custom domain pointed at Front Door keeps ordinary SNI and ordinary verification.
Only the standard HTTPS port takes the shared-edge path.
Cleartext broker URLs are refused outright before any front classification.

candidates_note: The discovery order a client builds from its configured primary. A genuine user override runs alone before the built-in fronts (override_first), so it cannot be starved by the defaults' stagger; merely persisting one of the defaults as the primary must not reorder anything.

candidates.note: Comparison is on the exact string, not a normalized URL, so a default written without its trailing slash is treated as a genuine override and is attempted alone first. Pinned because it changes the discovery order, not just the list.
